bull.b: Record revenue, substantial bookings and a large backlog provide visibility into future demand. This reflects broad customer adoption of AeroVironment’s systems and supports continued growth beyond individual contract awards.

A widening portfolio across lethal drones, counter-UAS and directed energy increases exposure to multiple defense priorities. Product milestones and manufacturing expansion can strengthen competitive positioning and support larger program opportunities.

The Greece joint venture creates a localized platform for European sales, production and customer engagement. Local manufacturing may improve access to regional procurement programs and support long-term international diversification.

bear.b: The sharp reversal from FY25 profitability shows that earnings remain sensitive to program mix, acquisition accounting and execution. Inconsistent margins reduce the reliability of internally generated funding and complicate sustained profit expansion.

Capacity investment may support future growth, but expected negative FY27 free cash flow raises funding and execution requirements. Higher depreciation and cloud amortization also create ongoing pressure on near-term earnings conversion.

The SCAR termination, impairment and control weakness expose risks from acquisitions, contract changes and financial reporting processes. Weakness in cyber and mission services further indicates integration and execution challenges across the expanded portfolio.
